prediction:
#41: the program-mode RADIAL fog coordinate is the stale fixed-function radial generator value, carried on the CPU. B carries the fix; A is its parent on the integration branch. Disc: Fog gen + Fog carryover + Fog coord vec4 + Alpha func, identical in both arms.

WHY THIS IS NOT #42, CHECKED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. #42 is "a program that does not write oFog inherits the previous value", and it is already fixed and verified. It cannot be #41's cause: fog_gen's vertex program is projection_vertex_shader_no_lighting_explicit_fog.vsh, which writes `mov oFog, #fog_value` from c[120], so pgraph_glsl_vsh_fog_write classifies it VSH_FOG_WRITE_CONST and #42's carried path is never selected for these draws. Silicon has a perfectly good oFog here and does not use it. Same not-cleared-register shape, one register along.

LEG A -- THE MECHANISM, MEASURED DIRECTLY, NOT THROUGH PIXELS. The B arm logs the carried coordinate once per distinct value under tag hakuX: `fog41: program-mode RADIAL carries coord=`. Predicted: EXACTLY ONE such line, with coord = 215.93 +/- 1.0.

215.93 is not fitted. It is the radial distance of the last vertex the fixed-function scene draws (quad 373's fourth, screen (368, 465) at world z 180.5), on a geometry validated against silicon's own FogGen_FF-linear-radial to +0.359 +/- 0.169 over 183 quads, worst 0.780 of a 0.784 step. The goldens independently require the coordinate to be in (204.06, 221.81), recovered by fog_radial_band.py. Nothing in the patch forces the logged number into that window: it is |modelview . v| of whatever vertex the guest's draw stream leaves in inline_value.

FALSIFIER (A). Three specific ways this fails, each a different diagnosis:
  - coord ~= 288.9: the label overlay is the last fixed-function RADIAL draw, so the shadow is following text vertices. FogGen_FF-linear_abs-radial's label ends at column 286, which is 288.9 in screen coordinates through the same modelview. Then the entry point is right and the gate is wrong -- one condition, not a revert.
  - coord = 0.0 (or no line at all): no fixed-function RADIAL draw reached the shadow, i.e. set_vsh_uniform_values is not the per-draw hook I take it for, or skinning is not OFF here.
  - more than one line, or a value outside (204.06, 221.81): the coordinate varies across the scene, which contradicts the goldens holding one colour, and the stale-register model is wrong rather than misplaced.

LEG B -- THE CONSEQUENCE. All six FogGen_VS-*-radial go from 181,016 differing pixels to 0. Registered as expect-value = 0 on each.

This is a real test and not a restatement of the patch, because the quantiser has to agree too: our fog chain reproduces all six goldens only for a coordinate in (205.43, 249.37], the goldens pin silicon's to (204.06, 221.81), and 215.93 has to land in the OVERLAP (205.43, 221.81] for the four clipped captures to read (255,0,0) and the two interior ones to read (254,0,1). A coordinate anywhere in the band but below 205.43 would satisfy Leg A and still leave the two interior captures wrong.

A residue under 1,000 px on the two interior captures with the other four exact is a DIFFERENT and much smaller finding -- the coordinate is right and psh.c's 2^x is a step off silicon's, which psh.c already documents -- and is reported as such rather than as Leg B passing.

NOT A FALSIFIER, and recorded as an assertion so it is not counted as one: "each capture holds a single mix colour". A carried scalar forces that. It is the patch describing itself.

LEG C -- MUST NOT MOVE. The new branch is taken only when fog is enabled, the draw is programmable, and FOGGEN == RADIAL. That combination exists in exactly six captures corpus-wide: fog_gen_tests.cpp is the only file that sets FOG_GEN_MODE_V_RADIAL with a program (fog_tests.cpp:25-30 and fog_exceptional_value_tests.cpp:98 comment it out, citing abaire/nxdk_pgraph_tests#214), and test_suite.cpp:274 pushes FOG_GEN_MODE = PLANAR in the per-test defaults, so RADIAL cannot leak into another suite. So:
  - the 30 FogGen_FF-* captures: byte-identical. Their shader is untouched and their uniform value is unchanged.
  - the 24 FogGen_VS-* non-radial captures: byte-identical.
  - Fog_carryover/* and Fog_coord_vec4/*: byte-identical. These are the captures #42's fix moved and they are the real collision risk, because this change edits #42's own update_carried_fog_coord to yield the shared uniform on RADIAL draws. If #42 regresses, Fog_carryover's eight exact captures and Fog_coord_vec4's CoordNotSet are where it shows.
  - Alpha_func/*: byte-identical, as the non-fog control that catches a build or disc mix-up.

WHAT THIS ARM CANNOT DECIDE, stated so it is not read into the result. Whether hardware's stale register is the last vertex specifically or a per-slot register file holding one of the last few. It cannot be told apart here: all sixteen vertices of the final four quads lie between 204.83 and 219.67, so every candidate in that tail predicts the same band and the same six colours. The single-scalar simplification is therefore untested at its edges, exactly as #42's was.

DISC COMPOSITION IS LOAD-BEARING AND BOTH ARMS MUST SHARE IT. The carried value only exists because all 30 FogGen_FF tests run before all 30 FogGen_VS tests on the same disc. On an isolation disc holding one VS RADIAL test the shadow is 0 and the capture renders unfogged, which is worse than A. That is hardware's own order dependence, not a defect in the fix, and it is why this prediction is void if the two arms' disc_id differ.
